title: Small-seq path architecture review - notes
content:
Context:
This was an architecture review focused on optimizations for small/short-sequence requests (1-32 tokens generated) where current runtime overhead and kernel selection hurts tail latency and increases cost per token. Many customer workloads (chat replies, search snippets, assist prompts) are dominated by short responses; improving this path has immediate SLO and cost benefits for hosted and dedicated customers.

Attendees:
- Priya Nair (owner / chair)
- Marco Alvarez (runtime / kernels)
- Evelyn Cho (serving infra & routing)
- Zachary Kim (benchmarks & telemetry)
- Lina Gomez (product / hosted API)
- Notes captured inline and action items assigned

Agenda:
1) Review profiling data for short sequences
2) Present candidate fast-path designs
3) Discuss tradeoffs (correctness, maintenance, quantization compatibility)
4) Decide experimental plan and owners for prototyping

1) Profiling summary (Zachary)
- Median request length for several PLG customers: 6 tokens generated, 9 tokens total (including prompt).
- For sequences <= 32 generated tokens: kernel-launch and dispatch overhead contributes ~45-60% of per-request latency at p95 on a 48GB A100 config.
- Continuous batching buffering (200ms target) increases latency for short sequences in latency-mode routes.
- KV cache warm path + attention kernel selection contributes an extra 4-8ms per request when verifying compatible quantization profile.
- Cost-impact: many small requests are not amortizing token compute; per-token CPU/GPU overhead is high.

2) Candidate approaches presented
A. Microkernel fastpath (Marco)
- Implement a specialized fused kernel path for sequence lengths <= 32 that: skips generic attention code paths, uses precompiled fused kernels optimized for short context lengths, and reduces buffer allocations.
- Pros: significant latency savings; leverages kernel-level optimization and fusion.
- Cons: maintenance burden; must keep compatibility across quantized model builds and multiple accelerator types; increased SMEM usage may reduce throughput for mixed workloads.

B. Lightweight dispatcher + kernel prediction (Evelyn)
- Add a low-cost dispatcher that predicts "short sequence" at request ingress and routes to a lightweight worker pool configured with low-latency scheduling (smaller batch horizons, reserved thread slots).
- Pros: low change at kernel level; matches SLOs by isolation; simpler rollout per customer tier.
- Cons: extra infra complexity, potential underutilization, needs capacity accounting.

C. KV-prefix dedupe + early-exit heuristics (Priya)
- Maintain a small in-memory prefix-dedupe cache for very common short prompts. If the incoming prefix matches and model variant identical, reuse last output or reuse KV state snapshot to skip forward. Also introduce early-exit when next-token distribution is confident above threshold to avoid full decode for obvious completions.
- Pros: great wins for predictable prompts (search/assistant templates); cost win by skipping compute entirely for cache hits.
- Cons: correctness risk, cache coherence, staleness for dynamic prompts, privacy constraints for shared hosted envs.

D. Sequence-length-aware kernel heuristics + compile-time variants (Marco + Evelyn)
- At model onboard time create an extra optimized artifact variant compiled for short sequences (smaller kernels, different tiling). Runtime chooses based on sequence length and model version.
- Pros: predictable; reuses existing model artifact flow.
- Cons: increases storage/serving matrix, more artifacts to manage for Dedicated/Private.

3) Discussion highlights
- Lina emphasized that product cares more about p95 and p99 reductions for short replies than raw cost reductions. Customers will accept a small increase in dedicated capacity if latency is improved.
- Marcos pointed out hardware portability risk: fused kernels must be verified across NV and AMD accelerator families; fallback must be robust.
- Evelyn highlighted operational simplicity of a dispatcher approach: simpler rollout, can use existing per-route scaling knobs and dedicated low-latency pools.
- Zachary asked about telemetry surface required to measure correctness/regressions for early-exit heuristics; suggested an EDS (evaluation dataset) per customer to track semantic deltas when early-exit applied.
- Privacy: for hosted API, prefix-dedupe cache must be implemented per-tenant and respect data retention/KMS. For shared pools, disable by default.

4) Decisions (consensus)
- Short-term (prototype within 4 weeks): implement approach B (lightweight dispatcher + isolated low-latency worker pool) and measure real-world improvement. Owner: Evelyn.
- Mid-term (research/experiment within 8 weeks): prototype microkernel fastpath (A) for the xformers-style attention loop on A100 only, validate p95/p99 wins and memory tradeoffs. Owner: Marco.
- Parallel exploration: build evaluation harness for early-exit heuristics (C) on internal EDS to quantify semantic regression. Owner: Zachary.
- Artifact management (D) deprioritized until we have data from B and A; but add a ticket to quantify storage/serving matrix explosion. Owner: Priya.

5) Experiment plan and success criteria
- Dispatcher prototype (Evelyn)
  - Implementation: new short-request route flag, small worker pool type (2-4 GPUs or dedicated slices), route selection based on content-length and model variant.
  - Success metrics: p95 latency reduction >= 25% for short-sequence workloads; no degradation in p50/throughput > 90% of baseline.
  - Safety: automatic fallback to main pool if error rate > 0.5% or p95 degrades.
  - Timeline: perf prototype in 2 weeks, closed beta with two hosted customers in 4 weeks.

- Microkernel fastpath (Marco)
  - Implementation: single fused kernel path for common attention config (block sizes aligned to 32, seq<=32), benchmarked on A100.
  - Success metrics: p95 improvement >= 30% vs baseline short seq; kernel maintains numerical parity within tolerated delta on sample evals.
  - Timeline: kernel prototype in 6 weeks, integration test in 8 weeks.

- Early-exit evals (Zachary)
  - Build EDS representing short completion cases, implement confidence-based early-exit in offline decoder for evaluation only.
  - Success metric: semantic regression false-positive rate < 1% on EDS; average compute reduction > 10% on EDS.
  - Timeline: EDS defined in 1 week, offline evals in 3 weeks.

6) Risks and mitigation
- Kernel complexity: keep fastpath behind feature flag and HW whitelist; maintain a fallback path that always works.
- Capacity fragmentation: dispatcher could cause waste; mitigation is autoscale tuning and adjustable pool sizing; measure utilization during beta.
- Correctness regressions: require gated rollout with eval dataset and per-tenant rollback; add regression alerts to Redwood Console.
- Security/privacy: per-tenant cache only, KMS-integrated ephemeral keys, purge policy.

7) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Evelyn: create dispatcher prototype PR and test harness (due 2025-03-04).
- Marco: spike fused kernel implementation and benchmark on A100 (due 2025-03-18).
- Zachary: assemble short-sequence EDS and offline early-exit harness (due 2025-02-25).
- Priya: create RFC summary and ticketize artifact management cost analysis (INF-1405) (due 2025-03-01).
- Lina: identify two hosted customers for closed beta and prepare customer success playbook (due 2025-03-10).

8) Follow-ups / next meeting
- Weekly sync focused on prototype telemetry: first sync 2025-02-25 to review dispatcher perf.
- Kernel review checkpoint 2025-03-11.

References / notes
- Baseline telemetry dashboards: route=chat-short, model=rwkv-small, timeframe=last_30_days.
- Related tickets: INF-1372 (short-seq perf investigation), INF-1405 (artifact management estimate).
- Example PR for dispatcher pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523

Open questions (to be resolved during prototyping)
- What is the expected utilization profile of short-pools under bursty traffic? (Evelyn to model)
- How much memory headroom do fused kernels require on top of standard kernels for mixed workloads? (Marco to measure)
- Acceptable semantic delta threshold for early-exit in production across customers? (Product + Research to decide)

Appendix: quick notes from product (Lina)
- Customers to prioritize: hosted chat apps, search snippet generation, light assistant completions.
- Pricing implication: if we add low-latency pool as a premium routing tier, product will propose a small surcharge for predictable SLOs.

End of notes.
